newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm on new orders, seen edging up.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm on new orders, seen edging up.

text.p: Some leading Russian shares opened firmer on cautious buying and traders said funds flow could lead to a slight rise for the day but said foreigners were still seeking out bargain rather than liquid stocks.
"I think there's potential for growth," said Prospekt's head of overseas trading Igor Lossavio. "There are some new orders -- people have decided to invest some money in Russia."
Shares of oil producer LUKoil rose to $15.69 at 0910 GMT from $15.55 on Friday, while Rostelekom edged up to $3.88 from $3.86. LUKoil announced a 1996 profit rise last week.
National power company UES firmed to $0.3170 from $0.3145, and Surgutneftegaz rose to $0.940 from $0.905.
Aton trader Alexander Bobolev said both Russian and Western investors were buying, but foreigners were more active in the less liquid shares trading on the second tier of the RTS.
"The market is limp...but I think the (upward) trend will continue," he said.
Lossavio saw growth continuing during the week but was cautious on the long-term outlook.
"People are looking carefully where to put their money," Lossavio said. "We expect growth (for the week) but we can't say for sure that this is the beginning of sustained growth."
